name: C# orders API
description: An ASP.NET controller with SQL built by concatenation, a shell command, MD5, System.Random tokens, BinaryFormatter, a file read from request data, disabled TLS validation and a hard-coded password. Intentionally insecure, for education.
expected: Findings from the C# token scanner.

fixes.title: Read the password from the environment
fixes.explanation: The password is no longer in the repository (rotate the exposed value).

fixes.title: Use a SQL parameter
fixes.explanation: The customer name is bound as a parameter instead of being concatenated into the SQL text.
edits: var cmd = new SqlCommand("SELECT * FROM Orders WHERE Customer = '" + customer + "'", conn);

var cmd = new SqlCommand("SELECT * FROM Orders WHERE Customer = @customer", conn);
            cmd.Parameters.AddWithValue("@customer", customer);

fixes.title: Pass the path as a single argument
fixes.explanation: A fixed program receives the path through ArgumentList; no shell parses it.

fixes.title: Use SHA-256 instead of MD5
fixes.explanation: MD5 is broken for security use. (A real password store should use PBKDF2 or Argon2.)
edits:
using var md5 = MD5.Create();
            return Convert.ToHexString(md5.ComputeHash(

using var sha = SHA256.Create();
            return Convert.ToHexString(sha.ComputeHash(

fixes.title: Use RandomNumberGenerator for the token
fixes.explanation: RandomNumberGenerator is a cryptographically secure source.

fixes.title: Deserialize JSON instead of BinaryFormatter
fixes.explanation: System.Text.Json builds plain data, not arbitrary object graphs.
edits:
var formatter = new BinaryFormatter();
            return Ok(formatter.Deserialize(new MemoryStream(data)));

fixes.title: Confine downloads to the orders directory
fixes.explanation: Only the file name is used, so '../' cannot leave the directory.

fixes.title: Keep certificate validation on
fixes.explanation: The always-true callback is removed, so the default validation applies.
